protocol.description:
This protocol lets an application register a global shortcut: a key chord that reaches the application while any window has focus, for example to start a recording or to talk while a key is held.
The application names the action and asks for a chord. The compositor decides which chord the action gets: the chord the user set for the action in the settings, the chord the application asked for when that chord is free, or no chord. The compositor tells the application the result, and tells it again each time the assignment changes.
While the action has a chord, the compositor sends pressed when the user presses the chord and released when the user lets go of it. A click is a release that comes soon after the press, and a hold is a release that comes later. The application measures the time between the two events. The focused client does not receive the key events of an assigned chord that has a key. It does receive the key events of a chord of modifiers only, because until the user lets go, the modifiers can be the start of a different chord.
A chord is written the way the CrownOS settings write it: the modifiers Super, Ctrl, Alt and Shift and one key, joined by "+", for example "Super+Shift+R", or the modifiers only, for example "Super". "None" means no chord. A chord that an application asks for must hold Super, Ctrl or Alt, so that no application can take a typing key such as "R" or "Shift+R" from the other windows. The user can set any chord in the settings.
Any client can bind the manager global.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_keybind_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory for crownos_keybind_v1 objects.

entry.name: invalid_identity
entry.summary: the app_id or the name is empty

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Keybinds made through it are unaffected.

request.name: register

description.summary: register an action and ask for a chord

request.description:
Register one action of the application. The compositor sends assigned on the new object as the first event.
app_id identifies the application and should match the app_id of its toplevels. name identifies the action inside the application, for example "toggle-recording". The settings store the user's chord under the pair of app_id and name, so both must stay the same from one run to the next. An empty app_id or name is a protocol error.
description is a short, human-readable text that tells the user what the action does, for example "Start or stop a recording". The compositor can show it in the settings.
preferred_keys is the chord the application asks for, or "None" or an empty string to ask for no chord. The compositor does not assign a chord that it cannot read, that holds none of Super, Ctrl and Alt, or that the desktop or another application already uses. An application that already has the chord it asked for keeps it until the user gives the chord to a different action.
When two objects register the same app_id and name, they share one chord, and only the object registered last receives pressed and released.

arg.name: preferred_keys
arg.summary: the chord the application asks for

interface.name: crownos_keybind_v1
interface.description: One action of an application, and the chord the compositor assigned to it. assigned is the first event. After that, pressed and released come in pairs, and cancelled can end a press in place of released.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the object. The compositor releases the chord, and no more events are sent.

event.name: assigned
event.description:
The chord the action has now, in the format the protocol description gives. "None" means the action has no chord, and pressed is not sent until assigned gives a chord again. The value can be different from preferred_keys: the user can set a different chord or remove it, and a chord that is already in use is not assigned.
The compositor sends this event after register, and again each time the chord changes.

event.name: pressed
event.description: The user pressed the key of the assigned chord while its modifiers were held. For a chord of modifiers only, the user pressed the last of its modifiers, no other modifier was held and no other key was down. time is in milliseconds, on the same clock as wl_keyboard key events.

event.name: released

description.summary: the user let go of the chord

event.description: The user let go of the key that sent pressed. The modifiers can be released before the key: the event still comes when the key goes up. For a chord of modifiers only, the user let go of one of its modifiers. time uses the same clock as pressed.

event.name: cancelled

description.summary: a press ended without a release

event.description: The press ended without the user letting go of the key, for example because the screen locked or the chord was assigned to a different action. A press of a chord of modifiers only is also cancelled when the user presses another key, adds a modifier, presses a pointer button or scrolls, because then the user makes a different chord. The application must not do the action of a click or a hold for this press.
